approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted, score-ranked survivors using connected-fragment crossover and local atom or bond edits, sometimes continuing through several mutations. It builds a fresh surplus pool, verifies stable canonical identities and selects evaluations by correlated samples from a Gaussian process trained on all earlier accepted scores. That model uses folded counts of circular molecular environments with a generalized Tanimoto kernel. Real scores update both the full learning archive and the greedy survivor population. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Its bond-change operator changes the order of an existing bond and cannot directly shift an intact side group to a neighboring aromatic position.
approach.novelty: Transfer the previously tested intact-branch relocation into this Parent's existing bond-change menu. Detach a qualifying acyclic side group from an aromatic carbon and reconnect the entire group to an adjacent aromatic carbon bearing hydrogen, preserving the immediate formula and ring framework. The local move is unchanged from the earlier binary-model experiment, whose average score fell despite some useful breeding ancestry. The new question is its performance with the current count-based selector. Current siblings change surrogate targets, operator credit or recursive breeding; this Child changes the available positional move. It carries forward the earlier one-atom and multi-atom failures and tests one complete transfer without importing another lineage's optimizer.

observed_bottleneck: The current code Parent n-62daf219c70a has no direct intact pendant-branch relocation in change_bond: every existing option changes one bond order. Its complete supplied baseline is macro mean 0.5956696497334577 with population deviation 0.02659287062806747. A read-only audit of its fifteen published Search task logs reconstructs every exact indexed input and selected bond for 7,992 change_bond calls. There are 7,072 source-opportunity calls with 21,324 directed source options, but only 929 actually selected bonds would have an expanded menu, containing 1,391 added options including 470 multi-atom options. These counts use the exact inspected n-2bb53b5f7b44 eligibility helper on reconstructed source graphs; they are potential menu exposure, not generated alternatives, novelty or labels. The actual Parent has 6,396 invalid and 1,596 valid checked bond-order returns, 69,600 admitted pool members from 75,961 outer attempts, 435 full pools, and 629 best-parent beats plus 258 incumbent gains among 4,350 accepted offspring. Missing one-step positional access, rather than an assumed score defect of any attachment, is the limiting behavior tested. Historical L01 n-2bb53b5f7b44 proves the local construction and evaluated use: 368 moves, 365 identity changes, 362 identity-changing pool members, 20 evaluations, 16 batch survivors and 14 later breeding identities. Yet only two of thirteen one-atom evaluations beat their best scored parent, both fluorine moves, and all seven multi-atom evaluations lose; the paired mean is -0.0015770554771336414 with seed changes -0.0014827306371569815, -0.02273793877397301 and +0.019489502979729068. That failure is retained. The changed conditioning context is supported by count removal n-e00db808bbb4 losing 0.051295849138213355 and composite-selector removal n-01b48dd09404 losing 0.12438789088524467 on the current Parent. Those controls justify retaining the useful current selector, without proving a relocation interaction. L07 n-3d7abb033a40 has mean +0.00285865261315299 but seed changes +0.01149105862766897, -0.04849818345599599 and +0.04558308266778599, only one best-parent win among 64 evaluated direct descendants, and lower whole-graph win count. L16 n-d46a62f1756e has mean +0.004339340888033338 with seed changes +0.026198442940039035, -0.005227484047426012 and -0.007952936228513008, four multi-atom losses and no relocation selected into a later current state. Neither is independent current-L01 support. The n-32ac3137615b composition remains partial because its rejection-triggered loop does not establish the ordinary-continuation identity.
hypothesis: Extend the current count-guided Parent's existing change_bond option menu with the exact inspected intact single-attachment acyclic branch relocation from an aromatic carbon to an adjacent hydrogen-bearing aromatic carbon, preserving the immediate branch, ring framework and molecular formula while exposing positional alternatives to the retained selector.

finding_summary.headline: Intact branch relocations produce five local wins and useful breeding ancestry, but the paired mean falls by 0.033336.
finding_summary.insights:
The current count-guided context makes some larger-branch placements locally useful: two ester moves improve their scored sources, whereas all seven evaluated larger-branch moves lost in the earlier binary-model experiment. That narrows the old all-loss observation without erasing it or establishing a general placement rule. Nine of the current thirteen larger-branch descendants still lose, and this complete transfer also misses its endpoint target. The bounded gain claim ends here; useful ancestry is insufficient to justify the addition in this composition.

Immediate conservation has a specific boundary. Thirty-four evaluated descendants retain the complete moved branch. In the remaining case a later mutation turns the moved ethyl ester into an ethynyl ester: the attachment remains, but its internal chemistry changes. The two terminal-best sessions with relocation ancestry both have lower paired endpoints, and their ancestral positional products originally tied or lost. Subsequent crossover and mutation prevent treating that ancestry as conserved-group mediation. The largest positive task-seed change occurs in a cell with no evaluated relocation descendant.

Expanding the menu also changes the probabilities of legacy edits and later adaptive search, so the negative conditional result belongs to the whole menu addition, not an isolated estimate for each move. The molecular report finds preserved reactive groups, difficult ring arrangements and unspecified stereochemistry alongside recognizable amines, esters and lactams. Formula preservation does not fix those liabilities. Earlier results from other optimizers, their partial composition records and shared-Parent sibling experiments remain separate; they do not identify an interaction with counts, additivity or universal benefit.
finding_summary.results:
All 371 selected relocations preserve the immediate branch, formula and aromatic ring framework and change molecular identity. They produce 365 pooled records and 35 evaluated descendants: 22 one-atom moves and 13 larger-branch moves. Thirty evaluated products are single-call edits of scored parents; three follow crossover and two receive later edits. Five direct products beat their parents—two methyl shifts, one fluorine shift and two ester shifts—and all five later breed. Nine evaluated descendants tie their parents and 21 lose. Thirty-two survive their batch, and 27 later breed in 1,878 parent selections.

The intended mechanism therefore activates, including the useful accepted pathway, while the registered endpoint-gain expectation fails. Complete mean final Top-1 falls from 0.595670 to 0.562334, a paired change of -0.033336 against the required +0.002 gain. Seed changes are -0.093470, +0.020583 and -0.027120. Ten of fifteen task-seed endpoints decline; five improve. Four task means decline and zaleplon rises. Macro population deviation falls from 0.026593 to 0.021727, alongside the lower mean. Every seed completes, every pool fills, and the active count posterior and real feedback remain intact.

molecular.headline: Intact positional moves preserve aromatic scaffolds and reactive groups; later edits can change the moved branch itself
molecular.overall_character: This assessment covers every supplied Child and matched Parent n-62daf219c70a Search trajectory: five objectives, seeds 0/1/2, 4,500 evaluated records per node, including 4,350 accepted optimizer products. Each task contributes 900 records and 870 optimizer products. Both Child completion and full Parent pairing are established in context.comparison; no trajectory is missing. All fifteen paired sequences differ, and shared molecular identities have consistent recorded scores. The supplemental r0018-03 Slurm accounting receipt records all three executions completed with six CPUs, one A40 and 16,000 MB. The supplied full-panel mean is 0.5623338336136934 versus 0.5956696497334577 for the Parent, with paired seed changes -0.09346978537803097, +0.02058252844250197 and -0.027120191423763984. These are existing evaluation results, not an activation or contribution verdict from this report. The actual molecules comprise substituted indole amides and ketones, linked nitrogen-rich carbonyl heterocycles, halogenated aryl amines, bridged lactams, and fluorinated aza-dicarbonyl frameworks. Across the fixed task order the Child median heavy-atom counts are 25,36,32,30,27, versus Parent 25,33,31,30,27. Ring-string presence ranges from 0.9575 to 0.9770 and aromatic-string presence from 0.9494 to 0.9690; these are molecule-level text counters, not geometry or aromatic atom fractions. The complete optimizer panel has median four perceived rings and three aromatic rings. Diversity across seeds coexists with repeated upper-score families within individual seeds. Apparent plausibility is mixed: recognizable amines, ethers, esters and lactams coexist with N-halogen bonds, O-halogen bonds, O-O connections, crowded or unusually bridged rings and unspecified stereochemistry. Molecule counts with N-X/O-X/O-O bonds are 1,132/112/316 for the Child versus 1,042/278/273 for the Parent; X denotes a halogen. O-O counts include aromatic-labelled oxygen-oxygen edges and should not all be interpreted as ordinary single-bond peroxides. RDKit finds unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2,257 Child and 2,408 Parent optimizer rows, although every digest stereocentre-marker rate is zero. There are 110 Child products with at most three heavy atoms versus 99 Parent products. No evaluated Child has a ring triple bond, compared with 17 Parent records, but the unchanged legacy chemistry still permits such outputs; evaluated absence is not generator or pool absence. Neither graph validity nor a conserved formula establishes a practical synthesis, stable geometry, safety or a preferred stereoisomer. Recorded positional chemistry is narrower than the whole output. Of 7,899 actual change_bond calls, 913 drawn bonds have relocation options, containing 1,347 directed menu entries including 462 multi-atom entries. Menu availability carries no new objective labels. The 371 selected moves consist of 234 one-atom and 137 multi-atom branches, spanning one to nine atoms; all immediate products change canonical identity and preserve the recorded formula, atom labels, aromatic ring edges and all heavy-atom edges except the specified attachment replacement. The immediate invariants were checked on index-preserving source/product graphs, not inferred from a name or parent relationship. These moves occur in 370 outer attempts because one attempt contains two moves; 365 final pool records carry a move, and five outer records are duplicates. Only 35 such pool records are emitted and evaluated: 22 one-atom and 13 multi-atom descendants. Thirty are ordinary single-call positional products of an already scored parent; three follow crossover and two undergo subsequent successful edits. Seven evaluated moves occur after internal failed primitive retries, which are distinct from later successful mutation calls. The immediate crossed sources and the unused menu/pool alternatives have no assigned oracle labels here. Evaluated one-atom groups are fluorine, methyl, chlorine, hydroxyl and bromine. Evaluated larger groups include methoxy/ethoxy, ethyl and methyl carboxylate, methylamino, fluoromethylamino and O-Cl branches. Five evaluated descendants beat their best recorded parent, nine tie and 21 lose; the one-atom split is 3/7/12 and the multi-atom split 2/2/9 for wins/ties/losses. All five wins are clean single-call products: two methyl shifts, one fluorine shift, and two ester shifts. This is evidence for particular scored positional alternatives, not a universal favorable placement rule. Thirty-two descendants remain in their batch-final population, 16 in the final population and 27 are subsequently used as parents. Retention does not imply a parent-relative gain. Thirty-three evaluated products exactly match their immediate relocation identity. For the two continued products, exhaustive graph correspondences across each checker canonical parse have one mapping at every boundary. The methyl move followed by an amino append preserves the moved branch and every immediate edge; its formula changes through the added nitrogen. The moved ethyl ester in the other product keeps its new attachment, but a later bond edit changes the branch carbon-carbon single bond to a triple bond, after an unrelated aromatic C-to-N replacement. Consequently 34 evaluated descendants retain the complete immediate branch and one retains only the relocated attachment with altered branch chemistry. Later cross-generation breeding ancestry is recorded separately and supplies no evidence that the conserved group survives into, or mediates the score of, a terminal leader. The original L01 n-2bb53b5f7b44 result remains a counterexample in its binary-selector context: only two of 13 evaluated one-atom moves beat their parents, all seven multi-atom products lost, and its paired mean change was -0.0015770554771336414 with two negative and one positive seed. The current two ester wins do not erase that result. Historical L07 n-3d7abb033a40 had opposing seed changes +0.01149105862766897,-0.04849818345599599,+0.04558308266778599 and only one best-parent win among 64 later direct descendants. L16 n-d46a62f1756e had +0.026198442940039035,-0.005227484047426012,-0.007952936228513008, four multi-atom losses and no relocation selected into a later current state. Those original allocation, neural-replay, protected-handoff and walk contexts are not independent evidence for this current count-GP Parent. The n-32ac3137615b continuation composition remains partial, historical catalog coverage remains unfinished, and shared-Parent comparisons do not identify a count-by-relocation interaction or additive contribution. This report describes chemistry and its evidence limits only. Reproducible read-only evidence is in .slots/r0018-03-improve-L01/molecular/: trajectory_chemistry_audit.json covers all thirty trajectory files, relocation_exposure_audit.json joins all thirty logs to actual accepted scores and reconstructed populations, and post_move_audit.json resolves the two continued products. Historical conditions are retained in historical_evidence_extract.json. The canonical response is the immutable brief's response_path; no competing staging report is used.

per_task.generated_character: Compact indole carbonyl families dominate the better products. The top fifty have 23-26 heavy atoms and three perceived rings; 49 contain an N-halogen bond. Seed 0 leads with a methoxy/methyl indole, a fluoromethylamino pendant group and N-fluoro carboxanilide. Its N-bromo analogue has the same recorded score. Seed 1 instead has an N-chloromethyl indole and N-bromo anilide with aryl bromine; seed 2 has an N-chloro indole linked through a ketone to an amino/fluoro carbon and pyridyl group. The last motif has unspecified tetrahedral stereochemistry. The median size is 25 heavy atoms in both Child and Parent. Parent leaders also carried N-halogen indoles, N-hydroxyamide or vicinal diketone chemistry, so the conventional aromatic framework and the concerning heteroatom substitution both persist.
liabilities: Amide N-F/N-Br and heteroaromatic N-Cl connections are chemically different from aryl fluorination; high scores and conserved attachment do not make them routine substituents.
Crowded amino/halogen carbon centres and some annulated small-ring descendants retain geometry and synthesis questions. Parent and Child both concentrate in closely related compact families.
missing_features: Tiny low-score products lack the combined indole/aryl surfaces and carbonyl arrangement found in the better molecules. Upper-score output has few alternatives retaining that arrangement without N-halogen substitution; the ordinary initial amide remains a counterexample to any claim that this chemistry is unavailable.
Potentially stereogenic amino/halo ketone products are not stereochemically specified. No preferred configuration or unseen target motif can be inferred from these scalar records.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxy indole carboxanilide scores 0.305105, whereas seed 0/evaluation 143 reaches 0.447848; seed 0/evaluation 166 replaces amide-bound F with Br at the same score. The intact fluoromethylamino positional change at evaluation 209 also ties 0.447848, showing positional variety without a measured gain. Conversely, seed 1/evaluation 31 is a clean aryl-F relocation from 0.363716 to 0.374373. Seed 2/evaluation 142 carries a moved methyl and a later amino append, scoring 0.368052 versus its accepted parent 0.405192; that loss cannot be assigned to the methyl position alone. Atomic fluorine in seed 0/evaluation 99 scores zero. Thus the observed gradient favors a complete compact aromatic/polar arrangement over fragments, but does not establish a unique halogen or attachment location as the missing answer. Recorded seed maxima, Child versus matched Parent in seed order 0/1/2, are 0.447848 versus 0.394051; 0.439907 versus 0.474117; 0.429560 versus 0.438973 (rounded to six decimals).

per_task.generated_character: The three seeds produce different nitrogen-rich ring assemblies. Seed 0's leader has six perceived aromatic rings, linked aza-aromatic domains and an N-chloromethyl dicarbonyl heterocycle. Seed 1 has a larger substituted aza-heteroaromatic assembly with two aldehydes, ether chains, imine substitution and a dicarbonyl unit. Seed 2's leader is smaller: 28 heavy atoms and four rings, combining an imine-containing annulated ring, fluorinated anilino group, N-chloroethylamino substituent, and a six-member ring with four consecutive aromatic-labelled oxygen atoms. Those three O-O edges are graph evidence of unusual oxygen connectivity, not evidence of a chemically ordinary aromatic heterocycle. All fifty highest-scoring products contain O-O bonds. The full panel median is 36 heavy atoms versus Parent 33; the upper fifty instead have median 28.5. Large linked or repeated ring assemblies are generated as well as the compact leaders. Parent high-score families included carbonyl/thione aza-rings and O-halogen or peroxide liabilities.
liabilities: Four consecutive aromatic-labelled oxygen atoms, N-Cl bonds and peroxide-containing annulations persist. RDKit aromatic perception does not establish aromatic stabilization or isolable chemistry.

Seed 1 also carries aldehydes, imine and N-O connectivity; multiple electrophilic or labile sites complicate interpretation of its whole structure. Size ranges up to 110 heavy atoms in evaluated output.
missing_features: Low-score fragments lack the distributed rings and heteroatom/carbonyl pattern seen in larger products. The upper excerpt lacks a broad set of conventional oxygen-ring alternatives with a similarly arranged polar/aromatic surface; this is an evaluated-sample gap, not absence from unscored pools.

Repeated large assemblies and the unusual compact O-rich family do not establish systematic access to modest-sized, stereochemically defined, chemically routine whole molecules preserving those feature relationships.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial substituted dicarbonyl framework scores 0.548381. The three different Child leaders reach 0.603712, 0.607971 and 0.626304, while chlorine at seed 0/evaluation 197 scores the 0.5 floor. Seed 0/evaluations 115 and 150 are clean methyl shifts on linked aza-aromatic frameworks, improving 0.593668 to 0.594224 and 0.597142 to 0.598218; neither requires a newly added functional group. Seed 2/evaluation 207 instead moves aryl F while preserving an O-O-containing ring and falls from 0.604815 to 0.590915. Formula conservation therefore preserves a liability as well as a pharmacophore-sized framework. The highest-scoring O-rich family associates with the score; its oxygen sequence is not independently shown to be desirable or synthesizable. Recorded seed maxima, Child versus matched Parent in seed order 0/1/2, are 0.603712 versus 0.856148; 0.607971 versus 0.624821; 0.626304 versus 0.617802 (rounded to six decimals).

per_task.generated_character: The better molecules already contain substantial amine chemistry and halogenated aryl surfaces. Seed 1's 27-heavy-atom leader has a benzofused oxygen ring bearing an ethylamino centre, a benzyl-linked second aryl ring and a fluorinated N-methylpyrrolidine. Seed 2 instead leads with an aryl enamine and an N-ethyl tertiary nitrogen attached to a tetralin-like ring system. Seed 0's aryl/amine polycycle includes a perceived four-member ring and a nine-member nitrogen ring, showing a different geometric liability. The top fifty have median 31 heavy atoms and two aromatic rings; all have unassigned tetrahedral centres. Both Child and Parent support aryl/basic-amine families, with Child median size 32 versus Parent 31. Neutral SMILES do not mean an absence of protonatable nitrogens.
liabilities: Unspecified stereocentres occur in 826 of 870 optimizer records. The leading N/O-adjacent carbon and fluorinated pyrrolidine centres require stereochemical and stability assessment.
Enamine, crowded aminal-like centres, small annulations and O-halogen-bearing intermediate families coexist with recognizable medicinal fragments; preserved formula does not remove them.
missing_features: The poor substantial sulfonamide/acid example lacks the freely basic amine arrangement present in the better examples. The generator as a whole does not lack basic amines or saturated nitrogen rings.

The upper families lack explicit stereochemical resolution at crowded O/N-adjacent and fluorinated carbon centres. More ordinary ring geometry at fixed aryl/amine relationships is incompletely represented among the strained seed-specific leaders.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Seed 1/evaluation 294 reaches 0.999981, while the carboxylic-acid/sulfonamide-containing product at evaluation 20 scores 0.000627 and the aryl sulfur-chloride product at evaluation 39 scores 0.000962. In this visible comparison, a substantial aryl framework alone is insufficient; accessible amine-bearing arrangements accompany the strong scores. A direct O-Cl-branch positional change at seed 2/evaluation 125 falls from 0.820606 to 0.711691 while preserving the O-Cl liability. An aryl-F shift at seed 1/evaluation 282 falls slightly from 0.996814 to 0.992164. These actual positions need not improve a strong amine scaffold. The recorded objective is not a measured binding experiment or proof of a specific pose or configuration. Recorded seed maxima, Child versus matched Parent in seed order 0/1/2, are 0.971902 versus 0.999999; 0.999981 versus 0.996975; 0.989186 versus 0.999993 (rounded to six decimals).

per_task.generated_character: Better products link ethoxy-substituted aryl or quinoline-like surfaces to N-methylated lactams, dicarbonyl aza-rings and bridged or fused polycycles. Seed 0's leader has 26 heavy atoms and four perceived rings, including two seven-member rings; seed 1 has a quinoline/pyrazole-linked bridged dicarbonyl system with 30 heavy atoms and five rings; seed 2 has a 33-heavy-atom conjugated fused lactam assembly. Top-fifty molecules have 25-33 heavy atoms and four to seven rings, without N-X, O-X or O-O bonds in that excerpt. This is a useful counterexample to claiming all high-score chemistry is dominated by those bonds. The complete output still contains peroxide and heteroatom-halogen examples, and 619 optimizer rows have unassigned stereocentres. Parent leaders also combined ethoxy/quinoline surfaces with medium-ring lactams; both medians are 30 heavy atoms, with changed connections rather than a missing ability to construct rings.
liabilities: Dense bridged rings and unspecified ring-junction stereochemistry complicate plausible geometry and synthesis even when familiar amide groups are present.
The ethynyl ester continuation is chemically distinct from its original ethyl ester; tracing ancestry or an unchanged attachment alone would conceal that change.
missing_features: Low fragments lack the joint aromatic and lactam/carbonyl architecture present in better output. The leading families give limited evidence for simpler, stereochemically specified alternatives preserving those relationships without dense bridges.

The emitted products do not consistently preserve the chemical group that was moved at the primitive boundary. Subsequent chemistry can alter a useful-looking ester while retaining its atom inventory and attachment.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl/dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.167839 and the leading Child molecules range from 0.220831 to 0.227792. Acetylene at seed 2/evaluation 278 scores zero. A direct ethoxy relocation of the seed 1 leader produces evaluation 300 at 0.221008 instead of 0.227792, retaining its polar/ring inventory but lowering the score. Seed 0/evaluation 290 is another ethoxy shift, falling from 0.216109 to 0.178173. Seed 1/evaluation 77 is different: an intact ethyl ester is moved first, then an unrelated aromatic carbon becomes nitrogen and the ester alkyl C-C bond becomes C#C. The evaluated ethynyl ester scores 0.162854 versus parent 0.171952. The attachment survives, but the original branch chemistry and formula do not; the combined loss cannot be assigned to relocation alone. Recorded seed maxima, Child versus matched Parent in seed order 0/1/2, are 0.220831 versus 0.225840; 0.227792 versus 0.221410; 0.223417 versus 0.226003 (rounded to six decimals).

per_task.generated_character: Fluorinated nitrogen-rich carbonyl or imino heterocycles dominate the better output. Seed 1's 27-heavy-atom leader has an N-fluoro dicarbonyl bicyclic core, a pyrrole substituent and a seven-member N/S-containing unsaturated ring bearing two fluorines. Seed 2's 29-heavy-atom leader instead carries an eight-member unsaturated N-containing ring with an enol-like OH, fluoromethyl groups and an N-F dicarbonyl core. Seed 0 leads with a vinyl/imino/carbonyl aza-ring system and a benzyl aryl carboxyl O-F group. Median size is 27 heavy atoms in Child and Parent. There are 577 N-halogen-containing Child optimizer rows versus 476 Parent rows, and 32 Child records have a ring carbon with at least two double bonds. Such graph counts include different local chemistries and are not a blanket description of all leaders as cyclic cumulenes. Parent leaders included a small unsaturated nitrogen ring and a difficult cyclic cumulene family.
liabilities: N-fluorinated heterocycles and the carboxyl O-F group are distinct chemical concerns from ordinary carbon-bound fluorine. The seven-member sulfur/imine ring and eight-member unsaturated N-ring require separate geometry and stability consideration.

Local formula/branch conservation can preserve reactive or strained motifs. The reduction in some Parent motifs does not establish their absence from generated pools or improved overall synthetic feasibility.
missing_features: Low tiny products lack the combined aza-ring, carbonyl/imino and distributed substituent arrangement of the better molecules. The observed scores do not identify a missing mandatory target-specific substructure.

The upper evaluated sample supplies few conventional peripheral and ring alternatives preserving those relationships while avoiding N-F, O-F or geometrically difficult unsaturation. The ester-position witnesses show that reactive heteroatom-fluorine bonds are not required for every observed local gain.
Potential stereogenic fluorinated ring centres remain unspecified; the trajectories do not establish which configurations would be preferred.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl/dicarbonyl framework scores 0.002094, the three Child leaders 0.415417, 0.631590 and 0.599589, and isolated OF at seed 0/evaluation 216 only 3.4438155512720535e-22. The visible gradient associates distributed fluorinated aza-ring/carbonyl arrangements with higher scores; fluorine alone supplies almost nothing. Two clean larger-branch moves are local counterexamples to the old all-loss multi-atom panel: the ethyl ester position at seed 0/evaluation 36 increases 0.014458 to 0.014790, and the methyl ester position at evaluation 279 increases 0.383989 to 0.396083. Another methyl ester shift at evaluation 282 instead lowers 0.379625 to 0.367845. Thus conventional ester groups can be kept intact while exploring position, with both signs of score change and no general placement rule. The stronger seed 1 leader is not thereby attributed to an ester relocation. Recorded seed maxima, Child versus matched Parent in seed order 0/1/2, are 0.415417 versus 0.651021; 0.631590 versus 0.487006; 0.599589 versus 0.720885 (rounded to six decimals).

transferable_gaps.evidence: This continues the chemistry gap recorded at n-c55c3d520a2c and reproduced in the current Parent n-62daf219c70a. In the present complete optimizer panel, 1,132 molecules have N-X, 112 O-X and 316 O-O bonds; the corresponding Parent counts are 1,042,278,273. An evaluated O-Cl branch relocation preserves that bond and scores below its accepted source. Upper families include adjacent aromatic-labelled oxygens, while other strong families have ordinary aryl amines or lactams without these motifs. These are observed structure-score associations, not proof that a particular liability causes the paired panel difference.
transferable_gaps.gap: Positional access does not consistently preserve a chemically conventional whole molecule; conserved branches can carry reactive bonds unchanged.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Broaden conventional peripheral alternatives while retaining the observed ring and polar-group relationships. Assess them with the existing task-agnostic feedback, and distinguish chemical plausibility from sanitization, identity novelty or conservation; a universal motif benefit or pool-level absence is not established.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The exact historical local law from n-2bb53b5f7b44 conserves all 371 recorded immediate moves here. Yet among 35 evaluated descendants, one moves an ethyl ester and subsequently turns its internal C-C single bond into C#C after an unrelated C-to-N edit. Its attachment is retained but its original branch chemistry is not. Another continued product preserves its methyl branch and adds an amino group elsewhere. Both are resolved through exact recorded graph correspondences across canonical parses. Cross-generation ancestry is less restrictive still and has not been atom-mapped to terminal chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: Immediate group conservation is not a persistent property of the emitted descendant when ordinary continuation edits remain available.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Treat branch integrity as a molecular property checked at emission and later reuse, with exact correspondence through parse boundaries. Keep direct positional products, later-edited products and crossed sources separate when learning from real scores; ancestor labels alone cannot identify a conserved-group benefit.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Under the current Parent, 365 relocation-carrying pool records yield 35 evaluated descendants: 22 one-atom and 13 multi-atom, with 3/7/12 and 2/2/9 wins/ties/losses against their best recorded parents. The two larger-branch wins preserve esters; other ester, ether and O-Cl shifts lose. Unselected alternatives remain unlabeled. The historical binary-selector L01 n-2bb53b5f7b44 had two one-atom wins and seven multi-atom losses; those conditions remain intact. L07 n-3d7abb033a40 and L16 n-d46a62f1756e had opposing seed signs and different retention semantics. Their results are not independent current-Parent support, and the partial n-32ac3137615b continuation composition supplies no complete transfer equivalence.
transferable_gaps.gap: The evaluated positional neighborhood is chemically accessible but provides inconsistent parent-relative gains across attachment contexts and branch sizes.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve source-specific accepted-score evidence for placement while exploring branch identity and local environment without hidden objective identity. Keep one-atom versus larger groups, immediate scored sources versus unscored crossed inputs, and pool availability versus real evaluation distinct. Shared-Parent contrasts do not identify interaction or justify an unconditional positional preference.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The absence of explicit stereocentre markers, already documented in n-c55c3d520a2c and n-62daf219c70a, persists in every current task digest. RDKit finds unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2,257 of 4,350 Child optimizer products. Several leading cyclic amine and lactam families have them; the molecules are not all achiral. The exact local move excludes an annotated root and preserves existing atom labels, so conservation alone introduces no new stereochemical specification. This is an evaluated-output observation, not an exhaustive claim about all unscored generated alternatives or stable configurations.
transferable_gaps.gap: The evaluated output does not resolve stereochemical alternatives for many of its saturated, bridged and heteroatom-adjacent centres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent and retain meaningful stereochemical distinctions where the generated geometry permits them, then let authorized feedback assess their value. Do not infer a preferred configuration from unspecified records or equate ring perception with accessible three-dimensional structure.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
